4:1.sourceText: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοὶ καὶ ἐπιπόθητοι, χαρὰ καὶ στέφανός μου, οὕτως στήκετε ἐν Κυρίῳ, ἀγαπητοί.
4:1.targetText: Итак, братия мои возлюбленные и вожделенные, радость и венец мой, стойте так в Господе, возлюбленные.

4:2.sourceText: Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν Κυρίῳ.
4:2.targetText: Умоляю Еводию, умоляю Синтихию мыслить то же о Господе.

groups.note: The articular neuter same expression becomes the Russian demonstrative with a particle.

studyHeads.note: The actual identity pronoun is the lexical head of this sameness expression.

unmappedSource.reason: The two appeals are joined in Greek with καί and juxtaposed in Russian.

4:3.sourceText: ναὶ ἐρωτῶ καὶ σέ, γνήσιε σύνζυγε, συνλαμβάνου αὐταῖς, αἵτινες ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ συνήθλησάν μοι μετὰ καὶ Κλήμεντος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου, ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐν βίβλῳ ζωῆς.
4:3.targetText: Ей, прошу и тебя, искренний сотрудник, помогай им, подвизавшимся в благовествовании вместе со мною и с Климентом и с прочими сотрудниками моими, которых имена - в книге жизни.

groups.note: Actual ναι is an affirmation. The full printed TR here has καί; the exact Russian uses an affirmative particle.
The actual finite third-person plural verb contains the meaning of striving together. Russian uses a participle and makes joint action explicit with вместе.
The actual first-person dative participant of the joint activity is expressed by Russian со with the instrumental.
One actual μετά governs the two coordinated genitive terms. Russian repeats the preposition for the same two participants.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek whole relative construction is recast as a Russian participle agreeing with им; no separate relative pronoun is expressed.
These printed articles have no separately expressed determiner in the corresponding Russian constructions.

unmappedTarget.reason: Russian supplies a connector before the adverb of repetition.

4:10.sourceText: Ἐχάρην δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ μεγάλως ὅτι ἤδη ποτὲ ἀνεθάλετε τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν· ἐφ’ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε, ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ.

4:11.sourceText: οὐχ ὅτι καθ’ ὑστέρησιν λέγω· ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔμαθον ἐν οἷς εἰμι αὐτάρκης εἶναι.
4:11.targetText: Говорю это не потому, что нуждаюсь, ибо я научился быть довольным тем, что у меня есть.

groups.note: A Greek preposition plus the need noun becomes a first-person present verb in the same explanatory clause.

studyHeads.note: The actual need noun supplies the lexical content of the Russian predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἐν introduces the relative clause expressing the situation the speaker is in. Russian connects the relative directly to довольным.
The Greek first-person copula expresses the speaker being in the circumstances. The Russian existential clause makes those things what the speaker has.

unmappedTarget.reason: Russian adds an overt object to saying.
Russian expresses what the speaker has; the Greek has a first-person copula in a locative relative construction.

4:12.sourceText: οἶδα καὶ ταπεινοῦσθαι, οἶδα καὶ περισσεύειν· ἐν παντὶ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν μεμύημαι, καὶ χορτάζεσθαι καὶ πεινᾶν, καὶ περισσεύειν καὶ ὑστερεῖσθαι.
4:12.targetText: Умею жить и в скудости, умею жить и в изобилии; научился всему и во всем, насыщаться и терпеть голод, быть и в обилии и в недостатке.

groups.note: The first actual καί adds the low-condition alternative. The complete printed TR has δέ in this location; Russian uses и.
Actual present infinitive ταπεινοῦσθαι expresses living in a low condition (functional passive, formal middle/passive). Russian uses an infinitive and prepositional expression.
The first actual περισσεύειν becomes жить в изобилии. The later actual occurrence separately owns в обилии.
The actual μύεω is a perfect passive indicative of being initiated or learning a secret. Russian expresses the acquired learning with a past reflexive-form verb.
Actual active infinitive of being hungry is expressed by two Russian words.
The actual additive before the later abundance predicate is realized after the overt Russian shared быть.

unmappedSource.reason: Russian uses a dative with learned for the first extent. The actual ἐν has no independent Russian preposition before всему.
The additive introducing the first pair of infinitives is implicit at the Russian list boundary.

unmappedTarget.reason: The Russian finite sequence supplies a common infinitive for the final abundance and want phrases.
